source: FAO Plant Production and Protection Division — Potato cultivation (illustrative smallholder guide)
spacing: 30 cm between plants, 75 cm between rows; hill soil as plants grow.
how_to_grow: Plant certified seed tubers 10–15 cm deep in loose, well-drained soil. Hill soil around stems when plants are 15–20 cm tall — repeat until ridges are 20–25 cm high. This protects tubers from greening and sun damage. Rotate with non-solanaceous crops.
harvest_signs: Harvest when foliage yellows and dies back, or for new potatoes when flowers fade. Cure harvested tubers in shade for 1–2 weeks before storage. Do not wash before curing.

stages.name: Establishment
stages.watering: Keep soil evenly moist until sprouts emerge; avoid saturation.
stages.nutrients: Mix well-rotted compost into the planting ridge; avoid fresh manure (scab risk).

stages.name: Vegetative
stages.watering: Regular watering during active growth; 25–40 mm per week equivalent in dry weather.
stages.nutrients: Side-dress nitrogen lightly at first hilling if growth is pale; follow local rates.

stages.name: Tuber initiation
stages.watering: Critical period — uneven moisture causes knobby or hollow tubers.
stages.nutrients: Shift to potassium and phosphorus; reduce nitrogen to avoid lush tops and small tubers.

stages.name: Bulking
stages.watering: Maintain moisture until skins set; reduce watering before harvest.
stages.nutrients: Potassium supports tuber size; stop nitrogen applications.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.watering: Stop irrigation 1–2 weeks before lifting mature crop.
stages.nutrients: No feeding; focus on gentle digging and drying.
